small_guidance:
- The conv3d kernel is the dominant cost: BLOCK_S=128 with one program per (N, OC, S-tile) gives 128*16*N programs but each does a full IC*KT*KH*KW=81 inner-loop scalar weight loads. Try BLOCK_S=64 or 256 with num_warps=2/4/8 in an autotune sweep, and add num_stages=3-4 to pipeline the input loads.
- Tile over OC as well (e.g. BLOCK_OC=4 or 8) so a single program reuses the loaded x_val across multiple output channels — this turns the inner loop into a small matmul and amortizes the input-gather cost dramatically.
- In `fused_post_conv`, drop the separate `stats_kernel` + `apply_norm_clamp_max_kernel` two-launch design and use the existing `fused_norm_clamp_max_kernel` (single program per N doing both passes in-register), since C=16 and S=14*30*30=12600 fit comfortably; this halves launch overhead and removes the mean/invstd round-trip through HBM.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite conv3d as an implicit-GEMM: one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile) computing a tile of shape [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_S] via `tl.dot` over the GEMM-K axis (IC*KT*KH*KW=81). With OC=16 the OC tile can be the full 16, BLOCK_S=64-128, BLOCK_K=32 padded to 96. This replaces the current scalar FMA inner loop with tensor-core matmul and is the single biggest headroom item.
- Use channels_last_3d layout for the conv input/output so the GEMM-K dimension (IC across kt,kh,kw windows) is contiguous and loads coalesce; weight can be pre-packed to [OC, IC*KT*KH*KW] at first forward and cached on the module.
- Fuse the multiplier + instance-norm-stats accumulation into the conv epilogue: as each (N, OC) tile is produced, multiply by `multiplier[OC]` and atomically/locally accumulate per-(N,OC) sum and sumsq into a small workspace, so the post-conv pass becomes a single elementwise (norm + clamp + mul + channel-max) kernel without re-reading the conv output for stats.
